messages:
maya_support: FYI - AcmePay (INC-3492) reporting intermittent 502s for tool calls to \"create_payment\" since ~03:21 UTC. Our logs show: 

```\nToolBridge: args parsing error - unexpected token \"\\\"\" at position 0\nroute=toolbridge-v2 request_id=req_0a1b2c3d\npayload: {\"tool\":\"create_payment\", \"args\": \"[\\\"card\\\"]\"}\n```\n\nMinimal repro attached below. Customer says it started after they upgraded their SDK.
devon_engineer: Can you paste the request-id and the raw request from the customer? Also which model/route they were pinned to? :eyes:

maya_support: Pasted below (redacted api key):

```\nPOST /v1/invoke HTTP/1.1\nHost: api.redwood.ai\nContent-Type: application/json\nX-Request-Id: req_0a1b2c3d\n{\n  \"model\": \"rwd-pay-ini-1\",\n  \"input\": \"charge user\",\n  \"tool_call\": {\n    \"name\": \"create_payment\",\n    \"args\": \"[\\\"amount\\\":100, \"currency\":\"USD\"]\"  // note: args is a string (double-encoded)\n  }\n}\n```\n\nmaya_support: Customer also provided their SDK version: `acmesdk-js@3.4.2`\n\ntess_infra: That `args` being a string (stringified JSON inside the json) will cause our ToolBridge to treat it as a scalar and then schema validation fails. We rolled out `toolbridge-v2` routing rule to increase tolerance for variant shapes yesterday — suspect interaction. @devon can you try repro?

devon_engineer: Reproduced locally with the exact payload. When `args` is a JSON string we hit the path that attempts to route by arity and ends up picking the cheaper noop-tool, then the downstream schema rejects -> 502. Repro steps:
1) curl with `args` as stringified JSON
2) observe router selecting `create_payment` but runtime `ToolBridge` gets a scalar args body

Quick mitigation options:
- Add an unwrap step to attempt JSON.parse if args is a string (low-risk quick fix)
- Rollback `toolbridge-v2` to previous routing behavior (safer for now)
- Ask customer to downgrade SDK or change serializer (customer-facing workaround)

sre_bot: CI/CD: hotfix pipeline created (pipeline #4678). Can do canary deploy to 10% traffic in ~20m if we want the unwrap. Or we can toggle the routing rule off immediately (instant).

liam_csm: LoMad: told AcmePay we'll have a fix or workaround within 1h. They prefer we do server-side mitigation.

devon_engineer: I pushed PR #2345 that implements `toolcall.args: if string -> try JSON.parse -> if parsed is array/object use that`. Added unit tests for stringified arrays/objects. Plan: canary to staging then to prod. If timeboxed, fallback -> rollback routing rule.

tess_infra: I'm going to rollback `toolbridge-v2` for all customers for now to stop the error spike. Doing that now. Will also enable feature-flag `toolcall-unwrap` in the canary group after PR is deployed.

sre_bot: Change applied: routing rule `toolbridge-v2` rolled back at 2024-10-09T03:36:11Z by tess_infra. Error rate on /tool-invoke decreased from 6% -> 0.8% in the last 5m. :thumbsup:

maya_support: Customer confirms errors stopped at 03:58 UTC. Marking as mitigated and will notify them.

liam_csm: Letting AcmePay know: temporary mitigation done (rollback), ETA for server-side fix ~1.5h, recommended SDK workaround: downgrade to acmesdk-js@3.4.1 or ensure `tool_call.args` is real JSON (not string).

devon_engineer: After PR validation, will ship unwrap to prod behind flag `toolcall-unwrap`, then run a 30m canary and enable. Post-deploy tasks: add regression test for stringified args in our eval harness, and add a note to model onboarding docs about tool arg shape expectations.

maya_support: Filing postmortem checklist and linking tickets: INC-3492, PR-2345, pipeline-4678. Next steps assigned:
- devon_engineer: ship and monitor
- tess_infra: verify canary metrics and revert plan
- maya_support / liam_csm: confirm with customer and close incident

liam_csm: Thanks team. I'll send a short customer-facing summary and schedule a follow-up call if they want deeper root-cause. :slightly_smiling_face:
